script: [serious] For almost sixty years, the U.S. government wouldn't admit Area 51 existed. Then, in 2013, the C.I.A. put it on a map. The document was the agency's own secret history of its spy planes, released after a records request by the National Security Archive. Earlier copies had the base blacked out. This one didn't. It named the facility at Groom Lake, Nevada, a dry lake bed in the desert, and explained what it was for. Testing the U-2, a spy plane built to fly higher than anything else in the sky. Insiders even nicknamed the place Paradise Ranch, to attract workers. And then the document said something remarkable. High-flying planes had an unexpected side effect. A tremendous increase in reports of unidentified flying objects. According to reporting on the history, the spy planes may explain about half of UFO sightings in the fifties and sixties. Aliens? No. Something almost as secret. Send this to someone who still believes. This is Dossier Decoded. Case file number thirty-two. A new file every day.
